# Week 10 Mini-Studio

::: {.callout-note icon=false}
[Back to Week 10 overview](index.qmd)
:::

This page follows [week10.R](week10.R). Focus on regression-based forecasting, variable selection, and harmonic terms.

## A. Multiple regression for `us_change`

Core objective: forecast US consumption growth using economic regressors.

```r
fit_cons <- us_change |>
      model(TSLM(Consumption ~ Income + Savings + Production + Unemployment))

report(fit_cons)
fit_cons |> gg_tsresiduals()
```

Then run the full model-comparison and scenario sections in [week10.R](week10.R).

::: {.callout-note}
## What to notice

- Which regressors are consistently useful across candidate models?
- How do AICc/CV trade-offs affect your final model choice?
- Do residual plots suggest missing nonlinear terms or interactions?
:::

## B. Harmonic regression for `us_gasoline`

Core objective: model weekly seasonality with Fourier terms.

```r
us_gasoline |>
      model(
            K06 = TSLM(log(Barrels) ~ trend(knots = yearweek(c("2006 W1", "2011 W1"))) + fourier(K = 6)),
            K10 = TSLM(log(Barrels) ~ trend(knots = yearweek(c("2006 W1", "2011 W1"))) + fourier(K = 10))
      ) |>
      glance()
```

Use [week10.R](week10.R) to inspect diagnostics and produce forecasts.

::: {.callout-note}
## What to notice

- How does increasing $K$ change fit quality vs complexity?
- Which model balances smooth seasonality and residual behavior best?
- Explain why harmonic terms are useful for high-frequency seasonal data.
:::
